# Prompting Wan image

Models: Wan 2.7. A good prompt runs about 900 characters.

Name each reference where the prompt uses it as `@{ref:<ref>}`, with the exact ref you pass; Sceneform swaps in the model's own token, so wherever this guide names a token (`@Image1`, `Figure 1`), write the mention instead.

Wan 2.7 image reads a plain description and follows it as written, so every choice you leave out is the model's.

**Order.** Subject, then setting, then style. For more control, add the camera, the atmosphere and the light, in that order. Say what the subject is doing and how it is posed. Camera words from Alibaba's guide: extreme close-up, close-up, medium shot, long shot; eye level, low angle, bird's eye, aerial; macro, telephoto, ultra-wide, fisheye. Light: sunlight, moonlight, backlight, neon light, ambient light. One light and one style per image.

**Faces.** Wan 2.7 takes facial structure from the prompt. When the user describes a person, name the bone structure, the eye shape (almond eyes, hooded eyes), the skin and the hair, rather than "a beautiful woman".

**Text in the image.** Alibaba claims print-quality text, formulas and tables in 12 languages. Quote each string exactly as it must appear and say where it goes and how it is written: write "Time for Holiday?" by hand in the sand. To change existing text, name the old and new strings: change "18" to "29" and "JUNE" to "SEPTEMBER".

**Edits and several images.** Up to four images, each addressed by its token in the sentence that uses it. Give each image its job and say which way the operation runs, because moving image 1 onto image 2 is a different result from the reverse: "spray the graffiti from image 2 onto the car in image 1", "the boy from image 1 hugs the dog from image 2". For a single image, say what changes and then what stays: "keep the style of the dress and the model unchanged", "keep the rest of the image unchanged". Plain instructions work for whole-image operations too: "remove all watermarks from the image", "reshoot this photo with a fisheye lens", "extract the clothing items and arrange them as a flat lay on a pure white background".

**Avoid.** Leaving the direction of a two-image edit implicit. Describing text instead of quoting it.
